block_summary:
**Triage Summary:**

This scan reveals three distinct vulnerability clusters, all with available fixes: (1) CVE-2021-40438 across Apache 2.4.25 packages (EPSS 0.944, KEV-listed), (2) CVE-2019-11043 across PHP 7.0 packages (EPSS 0.941, KEV-listed), and (3) CVE-2020-15999 in libfreetype6 (EPSS 0.929, KEV-listed), plus CVE-2022-23943 in Apache (EPSS 0.606, not KEV-listed). All findings are patched and exploitable; the PHP and Apache issues are actively exploited in the wild. The underlying cause is outdated Debian 9 base packages from 2017–2019.

**Recommended Action:**

**BLOCK this build and upgrade the base image immediately.** Prioritize patching Apache 2.4.25 and PHP 7.0 to current versions; these are high-impact, actively exploited vulnerabilities. If immediate upgrade is infeasible, document a time-bound remediation plan and escalate to the product owner. Do not deploy to production without addressing at least the KEV-listed CVEs.
review_summary:
**Triage Summary:**

All 20 findings stem from three distinct vulnerabilities across outdated PHP 7.0 and Apache 2.4.25 packages (Debian 9), each with available fixes. CVE-2021-44790 (Apache mod_http2 buffer overflow) is CRITICAL with 0.871 EPSS and poses immediate risk; CVE-2018-19518 (PHP 7.0 across 11 modules) and CVE-2019-0211 (Apache privilege escalation) are HIGH severity with strong exploit probability (0.940 and 0.895 EPSS respectively). The duplication across package variants (e.g., php7.0-* modules, apache2-* components) reflects a single root cause per CVE rather than independent issues.

**Recommended Action:** Upgrade PHP 7.0 to 7.0.33+ and Apache 2.4.25 to 2.4.38+ immediately. These are end-of-life versions with known, exploitable vulnerabilities and patches available. Block deployment until upgrades are applied.
